    Relations along quiver coverings #

    Proof of Proposition 4.1, Step 1: "Paths lift uniquely from a chosen start. Contextual mesh relations lift to contextual mesh relations with a common endpoint for all terms. Conversely every upstairs relation projects to one downstairs. The direct sum of the upstairs path spaces from a fixed start, modulo relations, is therefore the corresponding space downstairs."

    A relation system on a quiver is a family of morphisms rel i : s i → t i of the linear path category. Its contextual ideal is spanned by the composites q ≫ rel i ≫ q' (RelSystem.ideal). Let φ be a covering of quivers and let relations of the cover map onto relations of the base, every base relation starting at φ X lifting to one starting at X. Then φ preserves and reflects ideal membership (mapPaths_mem_ideal_iff).

    References #

    • Multiplicative bases and deformations of representation-finite algebras, https://github.com/haruhisa-enomoto/multiplicative-bases-deformations. Numbered statements cited here refer to it.

                  Coverings reflect relations. Let φ be a covering, and let every contextual relation of the base starting at φ X be the image of a contextual relation of the cover starting at X. If the image of f : X → Y lies in the ideal of the base, then f lies in the ideal of the cover.
